## What it shows

```{=html}
<!-- Differences, not causes; provenance, small groups, what the data can't
tell us. -->
```

- The figures show that there is a massive gap in how many females make over 50K a year compared to males. There is also a general age range where a majority of our data falls, in the 40s. We also see that, on average, married people work more hours per week than those who have not been married. However, there are less counts of married females in our data compared to males.

## Limits

- The data comes from the DOI. The dataset contains occurrences from 3343 males and 1657 females, about half as many females as males. The data shows us how many make over 50K a year, what kind of employment, education, and marital status; however, it does not tell us the exact job, the family dynamics, the area of living, or the presence of children.
